hints: Look at the name tri-glyceride and count the building blocks. How many fatty acids join to one glycerol molecule?
Remember each join is an ester bond made by condensation. How many water molecules are released for each ester bond formed?
walkthrough:
**Spot the building blocks**

A triglyceride is made from 1 glycerol plus 3 fatty acids. The prefix tri tells you there are three fatty acid tails to attach.

So we need to make 3 joins in total.

**Apply the condensation rule**

Each join is an ester bond formed by a condensation reaction. In condensation, an OH from one molecule and an H from the other are removed to form water.

$$1 \text{ ester bond} = 1 \text{ water molecule}$$

**Count the maximum water**

With 3 fatty acids, we form 3 ester bonds to the glycerol.

$$3 \text{ bonds} \times 1 \text{ water per bond} = 3 \text{ water molecules}$$

options.A: Correct and well done. Three ester bonds are formed between glycerol and three fatty acids, so three water molecules are released.
options.B: Too low. This would only join two fatty acids, giving a diglyceride, not a full triglyceride.
options.C: Too low. This would only join one fatty acid, giving a monoglyceride with just one ester bond.
options.D: Not possible for synthesis. Zero water would mean no condensation and no ester bonds have formed.
